title: Two Decades Later, Star Wars Fans Unearth a Wampa-Sized Secret in Battlefront 2
summary: After 20 years, one of the best Star Wars games ever made just got a little more legendary. A modder decompiling the PC version of 2005's Star Wars: Battlefront 2 has uncovered a never-before-documented easter egg: you can play as a Wampa. Yes, the towering, furry beast that nearly made Luke Skywalker its dinner in The Empire Strikes Back is now a playable unit on the forest moon of Endor. The discovery came from S1thK3nny, a modder working on a project to remove old limits and add new animations to the game. While digging through the code, they noticed a hidden trigger: create a new profile named 'Wampa,' load up the 'Hunt' mode on Endor, and suddenly the Imperial side gains a Wampa unit. Normally, Hunt on Endor is a chaotic clash between Ewok warriors and Imperial sniper scouts. But with this secret, you can stomp through the trees as the yeti-like creature, shredding Ewoks with brute force. According to Iamashaymin, lead developer of the Battlefront III Legacy mod, the secret was hidden deeper in the code than usual, which explains why it eluded fans for two decades. The easter egg only works on the PC version — console copies lack it entirely — and it's disabled in online play. However, you can still enjoy the Wampa rampage in local split-screen via the 2024 Classic Collection release. It's a delightful reminder that even in well-trodden digital worlds, surprises can still lurk in the shadows. So, if you've got a copy of Battlefront 2 on PC, it might be time to revisit Endor — and bring your inner Wampa.
why_it_matters: This discovery highlights the importance of video game preservation and the passion of modding communities; it shows that digital artifacts hold secrets that can still delight fans decades later, reminding us that exploring code can be as exciting as exploring history.

background_read: Star Wars: Battlefront 2 (released in 2005) is a beloved video game that lets players fight large-scale battles from the Star Wars films. The game includes a ‘Hunt’ mode where players take control of creatures like Ewoks against Imperial scouts on the forest moon of Endor (the site of the climactic battle in Return of the Jedi). The Wampa creature first appeared in The Empire Strikes Back (the 1980 film), attacking Luke Skywalker (the original trilogy’s hero) in an icy cave on Hoth. A dedicated modding community has kept Battlefront 2 alive for nearly two decades by altering the game and exploring its code. This particular secret was found by modder S1thK3nny while decompiling the game, and its depth was confirmed by Iamashaymin (lead developer of the Battlefront III Legacy mod). Deeply buried triggers like this show how carefully developers hid surprises, and that even players who know every corner of a map can still uncover something new.

perspectives.description: Fans of the game are thrilled to have a new, official-seeming playable character that adds replay value to a classic. The modding community feels validated, and the discovery strengthens nostalgia for a beloved game, possibly attracting new players.

The secret only works on the PC version and is disabled online, meaning a large portion of the player base—especially those on consoles—are excluded. Some might argue that such a deeply hidden feature wasted developer effort that could have gone into more accessible content.

Easter eggs like this are a tradition in game development; they function as a signature for the creators and a gift for the most dedicated fans. The fact that this one took 20 years to find illustrates how complex codebases can harbor undocumented features indefinitely.

This find encourages modders to dig even deeper into the code of older games, potentially uncovering more lost content or even mechanics that could be restored with mods. It might also inspire developers to revisit classic titles and officially acknowledge such secrets.
